M15 bar 105 (open 2771.06, high 2804.59, low 2769.78, close 2803.78) is a spike bar and bars 106-119 form a tight flag between 2762.93 and 2804.59 (about 1.5% wide) - a continuation shape inside the H4/D1 bull breakout.

The trigger is not at a fresh range edge: 2775.61 sits only about 30% up the 2762.93-2804.59 flag and the M15 has not yet closed above the flag top, so the same bars can also be read as mid-range chop after a spike rather than a confirmed resumption.

H4 follow-through is not one-way: after the spike bar, H4 highs 2795.00, 2770.03 and 2804.59 failed to hold above 2795 for two bars, and the last H4 bar closed 2775.61 in the lower half of its own 2759.63-2804.59 range.
Stale D1 context shows the daily breakout above 2557.46 is only three closes old and its last bar made a lower high (2645.88 vs 2700), so the larger breakout is not yet confirmed.
uncertainty: The H4 context was stale, so the decision relies on a fresh 120-bar H4 raw read whose final bar closes at the decision time; H4 follow-through therefore rests on one new bar.

It is unresolved whether the 2850 H4 spike is a buy climax (deeper pullback likely) or a continuing spike (immediate continuation); that distinction changes the expected depth of any pullback.
conditions_that_change_market_read: A close below M15 bar 109 low 2762.93 ends the higher-low flag structure and shifts the read to a failed break below 2804.59 and a deeper pullback toward the H4 spike-pullback low 2718.09.
Two consecutive M15 closes back below 2700.00 would reclassify the H4 breakout as failed and return the read to the old 2357.18-2700.00 range.
A strong M15 close above 2804.59 with follow-through would confirm the flag breakout and move the phase from breakout-spike toward a bull channel, favoring continuation buys on the next pullback.
A bear bar closing near 2759.63 (M15 bar 104 low) immediately after the trigger would mark the High 2 buy as failed rather than pending.
